record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: map-dependent summation process for degree recovery
record.original_question: Given a particular map f in C(S^1;S^1), or more generally in VMO(S^1;S^1), does there exist a summation process depending on that f such that lim_{epsilon->0} sum_{n in Z} n |a_n(f)|^2 sigma_{n,epsilon} = deg f?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.7. Given any f in C(S^1;S^1) (resp., f in VMO(S^1;S^1)), does there exist a summation process depending on f such that (5.13) holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$. For a measurable map $f: S^1 \to S^1$, write its Fourier series $f(e^{i\theta}) \sim \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} a_n(f) e^{in\theta}$, where $a_n(f) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} f(e^{i\theta}) e^{-in\theta}\, d\theta$. Recall that $\mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$ denotes the class of maps of vanishing mean oscillation from $S^1$ into $S^1$, and that the topological degree $\deg f \in \mathbb{Z}$ is well defined for every $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ and, more generally, for every $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$. For such $f$, one has the Parseval-type identity
$$\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} |a_n(f)|^2 = 1,$$
and formally
$$\deg f \;=\; \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2,$$
where the right-hand side need not converge absolutely.

By a summation process we mean a family of coefficients $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z},\, 0<\varepsilon<1}$ such that, for each $\varepsilon>0$, $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\to 0$ sufficiently fast as $|n|\to\infty$ (so the relevant series converges), and $\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\to 1$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ for each fixed $n$.

Question: Given any $f \in C(S^1;S^1)$ (respectively any $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1;S^1)$), does there exist a summation process $\{\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}\}$, possibly depending on $f$, such that
$$\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0^+} \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\, |a_n(f)|^2\, \sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \;=\; \deg f\;?$$
artifact.category_tag: Fourier series and topological degree of VMO maps
artifact.status_search_result: The question of recovering the degree of a continuous or VMO map $S^1 \to S^1$ via a summation process applied to the formal identity $\deg f = \sum n |a_n(f)|^2$ is documented as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems and in related literature on winding numbers and Fourier series. No published resolution has been located.

status_evidence.title: Winding numbers and Fourier series (arXiv:1003.5748)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses recovery of winding number/degree from Fourier coefficients via summation methods for VMO maps S^1 -> S^1.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses partial results but the general summation-process question for arbitrary VMO maps remains open.
